title: Efficacy of the Exopulse Mollii Suit on spasticity, mobility, and pain in patients with hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP): a double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover pilot study.
summary:
Aim of the Study

This study is intended to determine whether the Exopulse Mollii Suit can be used as an effective and well-tolerated supportive treatment for people with hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP). The results are intended to help better assess and further develop treatment options for HSP in the future.

In hereditary spastic paraplegia, or HSP for short, increased muscle tone, known as spasticity, is frequently observed, particularly in the legs. This can make walking more difficult, restrict mobility, and cause pain.

This study will investigate whether the Exopulse Mollii Suit can reduce spasticity, improve walking ability, and relieve possible pain in people with HSP. In addition, factors that may influence the effect of the treatment will be examined.

What Is the Exopulse Mollii Suit?

The Exopulse Mollii Suit is a full-body suit consisting of a jacket and trousers. Electrodes are integrated into the suit and deliver very weak electrical impulses to specific muscles.
These impulses are intended to relax tense muscles and support less active muscles. The application is non-invasive, meaning that no intervention in the body is performed. Each stimulation session lasts 60 minutes.

Study Procedure

The study will be conducted over several days. During the stay, various assessments will be performed to evaluate walking ability, mobility, spasticity, and possible pain.
Study Schedule

•	Sunday: Arrival and admission.
•	Monday: Assessments will be performed before stimulation. This will be followed by a 60-minute application with the Mollii Suit. Two hours later, the assessments will be repeated.
•	Tuesday: Further assessments, as on the previous day, will be performed, as well as additional measurements of the nerve pathways, known as SSEP and MEP.
•	Wednesday: Assessments will again be performed before stimulation. This will be followed by a second 60-minute application with the Mollii Suit. Two hours later, the assessments will be repeated.
•	Thursday: Final assessments will be performed in the morning, followed by departure.


One of the two applications is an active stimulation, while the other is a sham stimulation, meaning a placebo. The order will be determined at random. This means that either the active stimulation will be applied first and the placebo stimulation second, or vice versa.
During the study, neither the participants nor the study team will know which application is being administered on which day. This is intended to allow the results to be evaluated as objectively as possible.

Assessments Performed During the Study

The following assessments, among others, will be performed as part of the study:
10-Meter Walk Test to assess walking speed
Timed Up and Go Test (TUG) to assess mobility and balance
Berg Balance Scale to assess balance
Pain assessment using the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS)
Assessment of spasticity
Spastic Paraplegia Rating Scale (SPRS) to assess HSP-specific symptoms
Questionnaire on the Mollii Suit
Video recording of walking for subsequent movement analysis
Neurophysiological measurements of nerve pathways, known as SSEP and MEP

Who Can Participate?

Participation is generally possible if the following requirements are met:
A confirmed diagnosis of hereditary spastic paraplegia, HSP, is present.
A walking distance of at least 50 metres can be covered, with assistive devices if necessary.
Participation is, for example, not possible in the case of:
other neurological disorders
severe internal medical conditions
pregnancy
pacemaker
baclofen pump
ventriculoperitoneal shunt
BMI above 35 kg/m²

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
a. Confirmed diagnosis of HSP
b. Presence of clinically relevant spasticity
c. Ability to participate in the outpatient study on four to five consecutive days
d. Sufficient cognitive and language skills to understand the study procedures and follow instructions
e. Capacity to provide consent and written informed consent obtained
f. Preserved walking ability, with or without assistive devices, for at least 50 m
g. Age > 18 years
Exclusion criteria:
a. Other neurological disorder
b. Cardiovascular disease or other relevant internal medical conditions
c. Malignant diseases/cancer
d. Acute infectious diseases
e. Fever
f. Epilepsy
g. Skin diseases, rashes, or other skin problems in the area of stimulation application
h. Pregnancy
i. BMI > 35 kg/m²
j. Pacemaker
k. Ventriculoperitoneal shunt
l. Baclofen pump
m. Concurrent use of another medical device that could impair the safety or function of the electrical stimulation.
